clue.text: Having supplier of tickets and currency, set off to take short flight

parts.note: a buck is a dollar, a unit of currency

indicators.note: set off suggests the letters of set being knocked out of place and rearranged

parts.note: a hop is a short flight, as in a quick hop across the Channel

explanation.surface: A travel agent dealing in tickets and foreign money sets out on a brief plane trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET into ETS. 'Having' and 'and' are link words. A bucket shop is British slang for a cut-price agency selling airline tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket shop is an agency selling cheap, often unofficial, airline tickets, so it supplies tickets.

clue.text: So unpleasantly early an hour H G Wells's invaders appeared?

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling at an early start compares it to the arrival of Martians in The War of the Worlds.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'unearthly hour' is an idiom for an unreasonably early time; H G Wells's Martian invaders were literally from beyond the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an unearthly hour is ridiculously early, and Wells's Martians were not of this world.

clue.text: Unfairly criticise batsman's effort

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator is accused of being harsh about a batsman's innings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman's innings is informally called a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to knock something is to disparage it, and a knock is a cricketer's spell of batting.

clue.text: Two prizes lifted — that's high-class

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a reward is a prize
a pot is a prize, as in a trophy cup or the money in a game

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that winning two awards proves their class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns the whole run REWARDPOT upwards, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: top-drawer means of the highest social class or quality.

clue.text: Was obliged to cut fish

parts.note: had, as in 'had to', means was obliged
to dock is to cut short, as with a tail or wages

explanation.surface: A cook had no choice but to slice up the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the haddock is a North Atlantic food fish.

clue.text: Papers in the cupboard

explanation.surface: Someone says the newspapers are kept in the cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the press means newspapers collectively, and a press is also a large cupboard for linen or clothes.

clue.text: Two-note Portuguese song

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
do (or doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A simple Portuguese folk tune uses only two notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: fado is a melancholy Portuguese folk-song style.

clue.text: Well short of objective? By no means

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a target is nowhere near reached and answers with a flat denial.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: far from it means both a long way off the target and, as a reply, not at all.

clue.text: Caught in the sand? He never learns

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for caught within the sand word

parts.note: a dune is a hill of sand
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cricketer caught out on the beach is mocked as a slow learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a dunce is a slow pupil who never seems to learn anything.

clue.text: As compensation, got strawberry ice-cream dish included

indicators.note: included means the dish sits inside the colour word

parts.note: strawberry describes a red colour
a coupe is a shallow dish for serving ice cream

explanation.surface: Someone was given a strawberry sundae to make up for a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to recoup is to get back money or losses, so recouped means got as compensation.

clue.text: Wrong to be looking for adventure

explanation.surface: It is a mistake to go seeking thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' joins the two senses; a knight errant roamed seeking adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: errant means straying from what is right, and also travelling in search of adventure.

clue.text: Destroyed resistance agent

parts.note: broke can mean destroyed, as in broke the machine
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A Resistance fighter is undone in a wartime spy story.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a broker is an agent who buys and sells on behalf of others.

clue.text: I notice he died with cut across jugular in the end

parts.note: OB is short for Latin obiit, he (or she) died

indicators.note: across means the cut word stretches over the other letter

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word jugular

explanation.surface: A detective remarks that the victim died from a slash across the throat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: an observer is the person who says 'I notice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an observer is one who watches and notices, so says I notice.

clue.text: Time to put the squeeze on hooligan

parts.note: to hug is to squeeze someone in your arms

explanation.surface: It is time to clamp down on a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thug is a violent hooligan.

clue.text: Fighter rejoicing —— one taking part's knocked out cold

parts.note: glad means rejoicing or happy
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: knocked out means the letter for cold is removed

parts.note: an actor is someone taking a part
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A boxer celebrates while a rival in the bout lies knocked out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' removes C from ACTOR, leaving ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a gladiator was an armed fighter in the Roman arena.

clue.text: Public schoolboy's mistake — why, let it go

indicators.note: letting the letters go loose suggests they are freed to form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a schoolboy's blunder with 'why worry, let it go'.
explanation.walkthrough: MISTAKE and WHY are rearranged. A Wykehamist is a pupil of Winchester College, an old English fee-paying (public) school.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Wykehamist is a boy at Winchester College, a famous British public school.

clue.text: Grass speaking rapidly: that's the trick

indicators.note: speaking means a word is heard rather than written

parts.note: hay is dried grass
presto is the musical direction for very fast

explanation.surface: A conjuror talks fast to distract from the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: HAY said aloud gives HEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: hey presto is the magician's exclamation when a trick is completed.

clue.text: Hospital, one in new Roman republic

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital

indicators.note: in puts the one letter inside the rearranged word
new tells us the word Roman is made over in a fresh order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A new Roman republic establishes its first hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROMAN into MARNO, and I goes in to give MARINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: San Marino is a tiny independent republic surrounded by Italy.

clue.text: West End district short of a woman that's musical

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: Mayfair is an upmarket district of London's West End
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer talks about a woman in the West End who is fond of musicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is a wealthy area in central London; dropping an A gives MYFAIR. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: My Fair Lady is a famous stage musical by Lerner and Loewe.

clue.text: Our father may be in Lincoln

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their father might be in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Abraham is the biblical father of the Jewish people, and Abraham Lincoln's first name; Lincoln is also an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: Abraham is called father of the faithful, and Abraham was Lincoln's first name.

clue.text: Dynasty's characteristic quality

explanation.surface: A royal family has its own distinctive character.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tang dynasty ruled China from 618 to 907.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the Tang was a Chinese ruling house, and a tang is a distinctive flavour or quality.

clue.text: Her act is a revelation, seen at first by holidaymaker

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word seen

parts.note: a tripper is a holidaymaker on an outing

explanation.surface: A tourist watches a show that turns out to be eye-opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on revelation: a stripper's act reveals all.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a stripper's performance literally reveals her body.

clue.text: Macbeth to be produced in Athens shortly

indicators.note: produced suggests a play staged anew, so the letters are worked into fresh order
shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A theatre company plans to stage Macbeth in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts ATHENS to ATHEN, which 'to be produced' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and Cawdor, a Scottish nobleman's title.

clue.text: Lose head? Spaniard loses his

indicators.note: loses means the letters of the word his drop out

parts.note: a Spaniard is Hispanic

explanation.surface: A man loses his temper, and so does a Spaniard.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking HIS out of HISPANIC gives the answer; 'Lose head' means lose one's composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to lose one's head is to become flustered and frightened.

clue.text: Seaman has switched sides, the wretch

indicators.note: sides stands for the letters for left and right, which swap places

parts.note: a lascar is an East Indian sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who deserts to the enemy is called a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: In LASCAR the L (left) and R (right) swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rascal is a rogue or wretch.

clue.text: Use spades on bad track

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in cards
poor means bad

explanation.surface: A gardener digs over a muddy path with spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: spoor is the track or trail of an animal.

clue.text: Rhyming game for Chinese gamblers

parts.note: a Chinese gambling game whose name is two rhyming halves

explanation.surface: Gamblers in China play a game with a sing-song name.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: fan-tan is a Chinese gambling game with a rhyming two-part name.

clue.text: Memorable sort of present

explanation.surface: A gift is described as one to remember.
explanation.walkthrough: The historic present is the grammatical use of the present tense to narrate past events.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym and grammar term: historic means memorable, and the historic present is a tense use.

clue.text: Bring up — this?

explanation.surface: Someone asks if this is what they should raise.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the first: the back of a procession is what you bring up, so 'this' is the position at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym and idiom: to rear is to raise a child, and to bring up the rear is to come last.

clue.text: Well-bred teacher couldn't relax here?

parts.note: a snobbish teacher would be uneasy in a vulgar place, yet this staff lounge is where teachers relax

explanation.surface: A posh teacher feels uncomfortable in a vulgar setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'common' means vulgar to a well-bred person, but a common room is where school or college staff relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a common room is a shared lounge for teachers or students in a school or college.
